Name: Prohibiting the use of city resources to enforce restrictions on reproductive care.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to prohibiting the use of city resources to enforce restrictions on reproductive care
BodyName: Committee on Women and Gender Equity

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Women and Gender Equity

Summary: This bill would expand the existing prohibition on using city resources to enforce restrictions on abortion to include restrictions on all reproductive care, including abortion and assisted reproductive technology, such as in vitro fertilization.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to prohibiting the use of city resources to enforce restrictions on reproductive care

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Section 10-184 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 74 for the year 2022, is amended to read as follows:
§ 10-184 [Abortion] Reproductive health enforcement. a. Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
[Abortion. The term “abortion” means the procedure to terminate a pregnancy for purposes other than producing a live birth, including a termination using pharmacological agents, and any services related to such procedure, including pre-procedure and post-procedure counseling.]
City property. The term “city property” means any real property leased or owned by the city that serves a city governmental purpose and over which the city has operational control.
Reproductive health care. The term “reproductive health care” means any services, care, or products of a medical, surgical, psychiatric, therapeutic, diagnostic, mental health, behavioral health, preventative, rehabilitative, supportive, consultative, referral, prescribing, or dispensing nature relating to the human reproductive system, whether provided in person or by means of telehealth or telehealth services, which includes, but is not limited to, all services, care and products relating to pregnancy, assisted reproduction, contraception, miscarriage management or abortion.
b. No city resources, including, but not limited to, time spent by employees, officers, contractors, or subcontractors while on duty, or the use of city property, shall be utilized for:
1. The detention of a person known to have performed or aided in the performance of [an abortion, or to have procured an abortion] reproductive health care, or to have procured or received reproductive health care, unless there is reasonable cause to believe [the abortion] such care was not performed in accordance with [article 25-a of the public health law or] any state or local law that applies in New York city; or
2. Cooperating with or providing information to any individual or out-of-state agency or department that would confirm, deny, or identify any person who has received or is associated with [an abortion] reproductive health care that has been lawfully performed.
c. Nothing in this section shall prohibit the investigation of criminal activity which may involve the performance of [an abortion] reproductive health care not performed in accordance with [article 25-a of the public health law or] any [other] applicable state or local law, provided that no information that would identify any person associated with [an abortion] such reproductive health care that has been lawfully performed may be shared with an out-of-state agency or any other individual without the prior consent of such person associated with such [abortion] reproductive health care.
d. Nothing in this section shall affect any other law or rule of this state or this city that provides a person a right to any information or document to which they are legally entitled.
e. Nothing in this section shall prevent a city agency from cooperating with or providing information to any individual or out-of-state agency or department for scientific study or research being undertaken for the purpose of the reduction of morbidity and mortality or the improvement of the quality of medical care.
§ 2. This local law takes effect immediately.
